option.counterfactual: Every compact set that is the closure of a smoothly bounded pseudoconvex domain in complex Euclidean space has an Oka complement, even without a Stein neighbourhood basis.
option.approach: Investigate whether Oka approximation can be propagated inward from the exterior of a large ball across a pseudoconcave collar. Focus on how weak Levi degeneracy could be handled without assuming Stein neighbourhoods of the obstacle.

judge.reason: It asserts an exact ordered pair, which is a claim a team could attempt to prove. That pair is identical to the answer in e3.

options.counterfactual: An Oka exterior of a smoothly bounded compact domain forces the obstacle's boundary to be pseudoconvex in every complex dimension, including at points with mixed Levi signature.
options.approach: Investigate whether a negative tangential Levi direction produces a holomorphic family of discs that CAP cannot approximate simultaneously. The aim would be an obstruction using parameter dependence, since individual entire maps and bounded plurisubharmonic functions do not detect all mixed-signature examples.

options.counterfactual: Every bounded smoothly bounded q-complete domain in complex Euclidean space has an Oka exterior whenever q is smaller than the ambient complex dimension.
options.approach: Check the precise statement and hypotheses of this proposed complement theorem against the available records before using it. In particular, distinguish q-completeness of the interior from a stronger condition requiring an exhaustion on a neighbourhood of the closure.

options.approach: Verify the quartic domains' smoothness, nonpseudoconvexity, and 2-completeness in arbitrary dimension, then apply the proposed theorem for dimensions at least three. Together with the verified forward implication and dimension-two necessity, this would determine the ordered pair.

options.counterfactual: The converse implication holds in dimensions two and three but fails in every dimension at least four, so the necessary-dimension set is exactly {2,3}.
options.approach: Investigate whether propagation of full Oka approximation requires two strictly negative tangential Levi directions on the exterior side. The quartic obstacles have two corresponding positive tangential directions starting in dimension four, suggesting a possible dimension threshold.

options.approach: Try to prove necessity in dimension three using holomorphic surfaces rather than entire curves. A mixed Levi form there has only one positive and one negative tangential direction, which might permit a CAP obstruction unavailable when additional directions allow escape.

options.approach: Revisit the higher-dimensional Fatou–Bieberbach constructions and determine whether their two transverse basin factors can be assembled into holomorphic parameter families. Establishing that stronger property could prove Okaness for the quartic exteriors in dimensions at least four without assuming ordinary Oka coverings suffice.
